subject.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events

question: Should OpenClaw accept `rawBody?: string` as the plugin hook contract for `before_prompt_build`, legacy `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`, including the documented direct-user and steer semantics?
rationale: This is an additive but externally visible plugin API and security-boundary contract; code review can verify plumbing, but maintainers must choose whether this is the permanent plugin surface or should wait for the broader trusted-inbound contract work.

options.title: Accept after queue-order fix
options.body: Keep the `rawBody` API, require the active-run delivery-order repair and rebase, then review/land under the documented provenance gate.

options.title: Defer to trusted-inbound contract
options.body: Pause this PR and fold plugin hook raw input into the broader trusted inbound-decoration design tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95333.

options.title: Reject this API shape
options.body: Close or redirect the PR if maintainers do not want clean user input exposed directly on these hook events.

recommendation.title: Accept after queue-order fix
recommendation.body: Keep the `rawBody` API, require the active-run delivery-order repair and rebase, then review/land under the documented provenance gate.

likelyOwner.reason: Most connected in recent main history to both plugin/agent runtime direction and the touched active-run queue surfaces.
